technical_and_design_decisions: Capabilities (U1) are stored as three independent maps in channel config (channel, application, orderer) using protobuf for binary backward compatibility.
Each component (peer, orderer) is responsible for checking only the capability maps that apply to it; channel capabilities are checked by both.
Non-supporting binaries crash on channel join rather than attempt graceful handling, in line with the v1.1 simplification.
Orderers enforce that orderer-group capabilities are enabled before allowing application-group capabilities to be enabled, to prevent accidental forks during the v1.1 upgrade.
U2 GetTrxState is implemented as a read from the in-memory write-set already collected during the current transaction simulation; it does not require a new transaction lifecycle stage.
U5 MSPConfig is converted to an interface; the original concrete struct is preserved as a reference implementation to avoid breaking configtxgen YAML input.
U6 refactor replaces chaincode singletons with explicit instantiation through a context object passed via interfaces, enabling parallel test execution.
U7 test framework uses Go text/template to render core.yaml and orderer.yaml from the World struct values, writing to per-test temp directories.

U8 validation interface returns a struct containing endorsement policy, validation plugin info, and init/escalation flags; the '+lifecycle' chaincode uses a dynamically constructed signature policy with N-of-N orgs (majority equivalent for the participating org set).
assumptions: The baseline codebase is Hyperledger Fabric v1.1-era Go, with Ginkgo/Gomega as the test framework and existing protobuf-driven config infrastructure.
A single developer is responsible for all work; estimates include development, unit tests, and concise inline documentation but exclude large-scale release notes and translation.
The video tutorial (U3) is roughly 15-25 minutes long, uses standard slide and screen-capture tools, and requires only basic editing (cuts, captions, no animation).
CouchDB performance (U4) is captured via Go benchmark tests plus an orchestration script that runs configurable workloads; results are published as a markdown report in the docs tree.
The V1_1 capability encapsulates all non-backwards-compatible behavior changes for v1.1; no additional capability keys are introduced in this increment.
Existing test suites that previously relied on chaincode singletons will be migrated as part of U6; no external test fixtures are left in a broken state.
CI/CD, build system (Make/Gradle), and peer/orderer deployment infrastructure already exist and need no setup effort.

The '+lifecycle' majority-orgs policy is generated using a standard N-of-N signature policy over the channel's current MSPs; future channel-config-as-endorsement-policy support is explicitly out of scope.
All estimates assume a competent Go developer familiar with Fabric's common/, peer/, orderer/ and core/ chaincode packages.

activities.activity_name: Design capabilities config schema and protobuf
activities.activity_description: Define the Capabilities message structure in common/configtx protobuf to support three capability maps (channel, application, orderer) and versioned capability strings such as V1_1.

activities.activity_name: Integrate capabilities maps into channel config
activities.activity_description: Add the three capabilities maps to the Channel, Application, and Orderer config groups; wire them through the standard config value plumbing so they are persisted in config blocks and Genesis.

Add ChannelCapabilities, ApplicationCapabilities, and OrdererCapabilities interfaces in common/channelconfig/api.go with sensibly named boolean switches (e.g. SetChannelModPolicyDuringCreate, MSPRolesSupported).

Create the concrete implementations under common/capabilities/{channel,application,orderer}.go for the V1_1 capability, mapping each method on the interface to the appropriate value based on the capability string being set.

activities.activity_name: Implement crash behavior for unsupported binaries
activities.activity_description: In peer and orderer bootstrap code, detect missing required capabilities during channel/genesis block processing and panic with a clear error indicating the missing capability, per the v1.1 simplification.

Update the orderer config policy/filtering to reject a config update that enables application-level capabilities while the orderer-level capabilities are not yet enabled, preventing the v1.0 vs v1.1 fork scenario.
Extend configtxgen to accept capabilities definitions in configtx.yaml and emit them into the channel config; ensure configtxlator can round-trip the new values.

activities.activity_name: Unit and integration tests for capabilities
activities.activity_description: Write tests covering: capability parsing, V1_1 behavior toggles, crash on missing capability, orderer enforcement of capability ordering, and full network upgrade scenario in integration test framework.

Update docs (capabilities framework concept doc, upgrade guide, and the per-component code-reference pages) describing how to add a new capability and how operators should perform the rolling upgrade.

Specify the stub.GetTrxState(key string) ([]byte, error) signature, its lookup precedence over the regular state DB, and the interaction with the existing GetState semantics for the chaincode shim interface.

Add the GetTrxState method to the ChaincodeStubInterface and the shim implementation, sourcing values from the per-transaction write-set collected by the peer during simulation, including proper handling of deletes.
Add unit tests for read-your-writes within a transaction and behavior on missing keys; update chaincode developer guide and shim godoc to describe the new method and its RYW semantics.

activities.activity_name: Create slide deck for adding organizations
activities.activity_description: Produce a .ppt-style slide deck illustrating the conceptual picture: channel config tree, orgs, MSPs, and the config update flow when adding an organization to a running network.

Capture screen recording of the operational steps to add an organization (configtxlator, channel config update, orderer submission, peer rejoin) and edit into a coherent 15-25 minute video with captions.

activities.activity_name: Publish video and embed in docs
activities.activity_description: Upload the produced video and add a documentation page that links it alongside a short textual walkthrough of the same procedure.
Define a representative set of query workloads (rich queries with selector, range queries on indexed fields, paginated queries) and the metrics to capture (latency p50/p95/p99, throughput).
Implement Go benchmarks driving the peer with CouchDB as state DB, including a small CLI/script that seeds data, warms the DB, and runs each query workload in a controlled loop.

activities.activity_name: Run benchmarks and produce results document
activities.activity_description: Execute the benchmark suite on a reference hardware profile, gather results, and write a markdown report under docs/ with tables and guidance for interpreting the numbers.

activities.activity_name: Design MSPConfig interface and migration plan
activities.activity_description: Define the MSPConfig interface with the methods needed by configtxgen and the config bundle, and plan how to keep the existing concrete struct as a backward-compatible reference implementation.

activities.activity_name: Refactor configtxgen to consume MSPConfig interface
activities.activity_description: Update configtxgen to depend on MSPConfig interface rather than the concrete struct, allowing alternative implementations to be plugged in by callers or other tools.

activities.activity_name: Add programmatic channel config block construction
activities.activity_description: Provide a public Go API that allows assembling a channel config block without YAML, using builders for organizations, orderers, application groups, policies, and capabilities, and serializing through the existing configtx factory.
Add tests for the new programmatic construction path, an example test that produces a Genesis block equivalent to a YAML-driven one, and godoc plus a docs/ page describing the API.
Audit the chaincode package and its consumers to enumerate every package-level singleton variable, every Init/Shutdown entry point, and the test files that depend on the singleton lifecycle.

activities.activity_name: Refactor chaincode lifecycle to instance-based design
activities.activity_description: Replace package-level singletons with explicitly constructed instances passed through a context object, and add an interface that lets tests substitute fakes; ensure public APIs remain backward compatible where possible.

activities.activity_name: Update unit tests for new lifecycle
activities.activity_description: Migrate existing unit tests to construct and tear down chaincode instances explicitly, and convert tests that relied on global state to use the new per-instance API.
Run the chaincode integration test suites to verify behavior parity and ensure parallel test execution is now safe; fix any remaining ordering or shared-state issues surfaced by the refactor.

activities.activity_name: Design config generation from World config
activities.activity_description: Define the World struct additions and the mapping from World fields to peer core.yaml and orderer.yaml sections (MSP, listeners, BCCSP, ledger type, etc.), and decide on per-test temp directory layout.
Add a helper that renders core.yaml and orderer.yaml from the World struct using text/template, called from the existing test framework setup so each test gets a fully configured, isolated file pair.

activities.activity_name: Migrate existing tests to new setup
activities.activity_description: Update the network/peer/orderer integration test bootstraps to use the new helper instead of hardcoded YAML fixtures; remove duplicate configuration that previously diverged between tests.
Run the full integration suite to confirm equivalence with previous behavior and update test framework documentation to describe the World-driven configuration pattern.

Define the ValidationInfo (or equivalent) interface that returns the validation parameters for a chaincode reference, including endorsement policy, validation plugin name, and any lifecycle flags needed for FAB-13523.
Provide the implementation of the validation interface for user chaincodes backed by the new lifecycle, returning the policy and plugin info configured at approval time.

Make the validation interface return validation info for the '+lifecycle' chaincode itself, with an automatically generated signature policy that requires the majority of orgs to endorse, using the current channel org set.
Add unit tests for the policy construction, the '+lifecycle' special case, and the user chaincode path, and document the interface in godoc and the lifecycle design doc.
